claimText: Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria is the public-facing policy initiative.
approvedPublicWording: Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria is the public-facing policy initiative.
evidenceSummary: Recorded in the repository README and the evidence-register governance documentation as the public-facing initiative name.
limitations: This record identifies the initiative branding and governance position only.
reviewTrigger: Review if initiative branding or governance structure changes.

claimText: Dan Sonsie is the founder of Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria.
approvedPublicWording: Dan Sonsie is the founder of Carpenters for Housing Reform Victoria.
evidenceSummary: The founder designation is recorded in the governed register documentation for project governance purposes.
limitations: This record is limited to founder attribution within project governance materials.
reviewTrigger: Review if governance records are formally amended.
notes: Founder attribution is treated as a governed internal record.

claimText: Dan Sonsie is the evidence custodian for the Claims and Evidence Register.
approvedPublicWording: Dan Sonsie is the evidence custodian for the Claims and Evidence Register.
evidenceSummary: The evidence-custodian role is explicitly recorded in the evidence README, register document and ADR.
limitations: This record governs custodianship and does not by itself approve any specific claim for publication.
reviewTrigger: Review if register governance roles change.
notes: Custodianship remains separate from publication approval decisions.

claimText: Sonsie Enterprises Pty Ltd is the nominated owner of the website, source code, evidence architecture, documentation and associated intellectual property, subject to any later express written agreement.
approvedPublicWording: Sonsie Enterprises Pty Ltd is recorded as the nominated owner of the website, source code, evidence architecture, documentation and associated intellectual property, subject to any later express written agreement.
evidenceSummary: Recorded as the approved governance and ownership position in the evidence README, register document, ADR and existing rights notice.
limitations: This is an owner-declared governance record for project administration and publication control. It is not recorded as independent legal advice or an independently verified legal conclusion.
prohibitedWording: The ownership position has been independently verified as a legal conclusion.
requiredNextEvidence: Maintain any later express written agreement as a controlled documentary source if governance or ownership designations change.
reviewTrigger: Review if a later written agreement changes asset or IP ownership designations.
notes: Public wording must remain cautious and governance-based.

claimText: The internal register and filtered public register serve different publication and confidentiality purposes.
approvedPublicWording: The full register is maintained internally, with only approved publication-safe material intended for public release.
evidenceSummary: The evidence README, ADR and governed register document all state that the complete register remains internal and only filtered publication-safe material may be surfaced publicly.
limitations: A public release still requires separate publication review and filtering decisions for each record.
reviewTrigger: Review if publication controls or confidentiality rules are amended.
notes: Supports the distinction between internal governance records and filtered public material.

claimText: Victoria is expanding the building-industry registration framework to broaden the range of practitioners required to be registered.
approvedPublicWording: Current Victorian building reform states that practitioner registration is being expanded to include a broader set of practitioner roles.
evidenceSummary: The Victorian Government building-reform page describes expansion of practitioner registration beyond existing settings.
limitations: This claim records policy direction in current reform materials and does not by itself establish final implementation settings or coverage for any future RRC model.
reviewTrigger: Review if Victorian Government registration-reform settings are updated or superseded.

claimText: The stated objectives of expanded registration include stronger regulatory oversight, practitioner accountability, consumer protection and restriction of regulated work to qualified, competent practitioners.
approvedPublicWording: Victorian reform materials describe expanded registration objectives including stronger oversight, accountability and consumer protection, with regulated work linked to qualified and competent practitioners.
evidenceSummary: The Victorian Government building-reform page states consumer-protection, oversight and accountability objectives linked to practitioner competence.
limitations: This claim is limited to published objectives and does not imply that government has made a final decision about any specific RRC pathway design.
reviewTrigger: Review if published reform objectives are amended.

claimText: Building consultants and site supervisors are among practitioner categories being considered for registration.
approvedPublicWording: Victorian reform materials identify building consultants and site supervisors among categories being considered within expanded registration settings.
evidenceSummary: The Victorian Government building-reform page identifies building consultants and site supervisors as practitioner categories within expansion scope.
limitations: This claim does not imply that comparable treatment has already been determined for advanced renovation carpentry.
reviewTrigger: Review if practitioner categories under consideration are revised.

claimText: Victoria is introducing information statements for building surveyors in response to concerns about consumer understanding of practitioner roles and functions.
approvedPublicWording: Victorian reform settings include information-statement measures for building surveyors to support clearer consumer understanding of roles and functions.
evidenceSummary: The Victorian Government building-reform page includes information-statement measures for building surveyors linked to consumer role clarity.
limitations: This claim is role-information specific and should not be represented as direct support for a predetermined RRC model outcome.
reviewTrigger: Review if information-statement requirements are changed.

claimText: From 1 February 2027, specified new Class 1b, 2 and 3 buildings will require a building manual containing key design, construction and subsequent-works information.
approvedPublicWording: Victorian reform materials state that from 1 February 2027 a building-manual requirement applies to specified new Class 1b, 2 and 3 buildings.
evidenceSummary: The Victorian Government building-reform page includes a building-manual requirement for specified new Class 1b/2/3 buildings from 1 February 2027.
limitations: This requirement must not be represented as a general requirement for Class 1a residential renovation work.
prohibitedWording: The Class 1b/2/3 building-manual requirement applies generally to Class 1a residential renovation work.
reviewTrigger: Review if commencement date, covered classes or scope settings change.

claimText: Victorian building reform provides useful policy precedent for persistent building information as a lifecycle-management and consumer-information tool.
approvedPublicWording: The Victorian building-manual reform direction is a useful policy precedent for persistent project information; it is not evidence of a universal requirement across all residential classes.
evidenceSummary: Interpretive claim drawn from published building-manual reforms for specified classes.
limitations: Supported interpretation only. It does not establish a universal legal requirement and must not be represented as applying generally to Class 1a renovation work.
requiredNextEvidence: Government advice on whether any comparable persistent-information settings should be considered for advanced renovation pathways.
reviewTrigger: Review if persistent-information reforms are expanded or narrowed.

claimText: The Victorian cladding risk mitigation framework permits an acceptable risk outcome without necessarily requiring complete removal and replacement of all combustible cladding and gives preference to evidence-based interventions.
approvedPublicWording: The cladding risk mitigation framework adopts an acceptable-risk approach and allows proportionate interventions where they achieve the required risk outcome.
evidenceSummary: Framework sections describe acceptable-risk outcomes and intervention pathways that may include partial or alternative risk-mitigation measures.
limitations: Cladding-specific framework for relevant buildings. Do not apply its legal or technical provisions to Class 1 renovation carpentry.
prohibitedWording: The cladding framework legally governs ordinary Class 1 renovation carpentry.
reviewTrigger: Review if cladding framework policy or relevant-building scope is amended.

claimText: The framework provides useful policy precedent for proportionate, evidence-based regulatory intervention rather than automatic blanket remediation.
approvedPublicWording: The cladding framework provides a policy precedent for proportionate, evidence-based intervention design in its own regulatory context.
evidenceSummary: Interpretive claim from the cladding framework's risk-based intervention architecture.
limitations: Supported interpretation only. Cladding-framework settings remain specific to relevant buildings and combustible-cladding risk.
requiredNextEvidence: Government evidence on where proportionate-intervention logic can or cannot transfer beyond cladding policy settings.
reviewTrigger: Review if framework intervention principles materially change.
notes: Policy-precedent interpretation, not cross-context legal transfer.

claimText: BPC rectification orders may direct builders, subcontractors and developers to rectify poor work during construction and up to 10 years after practical completion.
approvedPublicWording: Victorian reform materials describe rectification-order powers that can apply during construction and for up to 10 years after practical completion.
evidenceSummary: The Victorian Government building-reform page describes BPC rectification-order powers with post-completion duration settings.
limitations: Do not infer identical liability, enforcement or recourse settings for any future RRC pathway from this claim alone.
requiredNextEvidence: Any future RRC enforcement or liability settings require separate government and legal determination.
reviewTrigger: Review if rectification-order powers or duration settings are revised.
notes: Rectification-order claim only; no automatic transfer to RRC settings.
